title: Decision graph for observability redaction + tenant sampling
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a deterministic redaction decision graph that runs at trace/span ingestion time and emits a compact policy tag describing the action taken (mask/pseudonymize/encrypt/drop/route-to-private). The graph combines tenant policy, data sensitivity classifier, retention bucket, and active overrides. This ticket covers: (1) the decision graph spec and policy ID format, (2) trace/span hook integration to attach policy tags and redaction diffs, (3) telemetry (metrics + logs) to measure redaction cost and failure modes, and (4) a tenant-sampling canary rollout path to validate correctness and performance under live load.
acceptance_criteria: Decision graph spec document reviewed and approved by Security & Compliance
Trace/span ingestion adds a policy_id tag and a redaction_action field to spans without increasing median trace ingestion latency by >5ms for 95th percentile path
Logs pipeline produces per-tenant metrics: redaction_actions_count, redaction_failures, average_redaction_time_ms
Canary plan defined: 5% of tenants in QA, 1% of production tenants with monitoring and auto-rollback on error-rate spike
Audit logs include a tamper-evident record of the policy_id, the classifier score, and KMS key id when encryption is used
End-to-end tests that validate masking, pseudonymization (SHA256 salted), and encryption paths run in CI and pass
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff meeting with Security, Observability, and Data Platform. Agreed to use a compact policy_id (8 byte base62) to avoid cost on tags
2026-03-02: Prototype of decision graph implemented in TypeScript (ingestion sidecar) - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/1421
2026-03-04: Benchmarks show masking path adds ~1.8ms median and encryption path adds ~12ms median on p3.2xlarge; need optimizations for encryption hot-path
2026-03-06: Design review feedback from Compliance: require KMS key rotation support and key id propagation to audit logs
2026-03-09: Implemented span-tagging hook and added metric counters to forwarder. End-to-end test added for pseudonymization with tenant-specific salt
decisions: Use deterministic decision graph executed at ingestion time rather than post-processing to avoid inconsistent views across consumers
Pseudonymization will use SHA256 with tenant-bound salt and a stable prefix to allow safe joining within the tenant (no cross-tenant joins)
Encryption of high-sensitivity fields will use envelope encryption with KMS; KMS key id recorded in audit trail
Sampling strategy for early canary: 1% prod tenants, selected deterministically by tenant id mod N to make rollbacks simple
Store redaction diffs for 7 days in ephemeral bucket for debugging, then purge; long-term storage only retains policy_id and audit record
tradeoffs: Performance vs completeness: full-content classification is more accurate but adds latency; we favour a two-tier approach (fast ruleset first, classifier fallback asynchronously)
Storage costs: storing diffs for debugging increases S3 cost; limited to 7 days and access gated by RBAC
Operational complexity: integrating KMS per-tenant increases key management work; decided to start with org-level keys and roadmap tenant-key-per-tenant for high-tier customers
notes: Next steps: micro-optimizations for encryption hot-path (native crypto bindings), wire up KMS key rotation, and schedule a 2-week canary with on-call coverage. Coordinate with Platform to expose policy_id in billing/usage snapshots for audit purposes.
